items.title: Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Plant Worker Killed in Drone Attack, IAEA Says
items.description: An employee of the nearby Zaporizhzhia thermal power plant, a conventional fossil-fuel power station, was also killed by a drone on Monday, the IAEA said.

items.title: The closure of 'Novaya Gazeta,' the end of a beacon for the 'other Russia'
items.description: The newspaper founded by Nobel Peace Prize laureate Dmitry Muratov ceases to exist on Monday, November 9. Under Kremlin pressure, its journalists had managed to keep the paper afloat since the outset of the war in Ukraine in 2022.

items.title: Security Council LIVE: Strikes on Ukraine’s power grid, as peace talks loom
items.description: The Security Council is meeting in New York on Ukraine. Russian strikes on energy infrastructure are threatening millions with another cold, dark winter, and civilian deaths are climbing sharply. The meeting comes on the eve of US-backed talks due to take place in Abu Dhabi. Follow our live meeting coverage below.

items.title: Four killed in Gaza after sand embankment collapses onto tents, health ministry says
items.description: Three children are among those killed in the incident that came a day after heavy rain reportedly flooded tens of thousands of tents across Gaza.

items.title: The world's largest telecoms firm is on trial and the outcome has global implications
items.description: Huawei, the world's biggest telecommunications company, is on trial in New York, accused of stealing American technology and evading US sanctions.

items.title: Ukraine Hopes Oleshky Can Serve As Model For Wider Truce, Delegation Says In DC
items.description: Ukraine hopes a temporary cease-fire that enabled humanitarian aid deliveries and civilian evacuations from the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky could serve as a model for wider de-escalation efforts, Ukrainian officials said on November 6.
